releases.displayName: Patch Notes: Hypercar Expansion Pack DLC

items.text: Hello Racers!

This latest expansion of RENNSPORT brings four premier-class prototypes to the front of the field, backed by a class-wide Hypercar rework to give modern endurance racing the depth and feeling it deserves.
More importantly, this patch delivers the engineering fixes you asked for in Community Debrief #3—sharper console visuals, proper direct-drive wheel profiles, and 24-car multiplayer grids.
Scheduled for release on Friday 23rd October at 10:00 CEST, here is a breakdown of what’s included in this update and how these changes impact your time on track.
Based on your feedback from our recent community survey, we are shifting toward cohesive, multi-manufacturer paddocks with a unified Balance of Performance.
This paid DLC pack adds four brand-new Hypercars to RENNSPORT, including three new manufacturers:

Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR-LMH: A raw aerodynamic sculpture built around a bespoke, naturally aspirated 6.5-litre Cosworth V12. It demands absolute commitment through high-speed sweeps and rewards drivers who keep the rear wing planted.

Lamborghini SC63: Squadra Corse’s dedicated endurance weapon. Powered by a bespoke 3.8-litre twin-turbo V8, it is tuned for precise front-axle turn-in and predictable mechanical balance through technical mid-speed complexes.

Toyota TR010 Hybrid: The benchmark of contemporary prototype stamina. Pairing a twin-turbo V6 with hybrid electric deployment, it delivers relentless traction out of low-speed exits and proven Le Mans-winning consistency.

Genesis GMR-001: The arrival of a bold new factory programme into premier sports car competition. Featuring a twin-turbocharged V8 hybrid powertrain in a lightweight chassis, it represents an ambitious clean-sheet design aimed squarely at the established guard.

Alongside these four cars, the entire Hypercar division receives an updated tyre model as well as reworked engine power, aerodynamics, setup and balancing to allow for even closer racing in history's most competitive endurance machines.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/dca7ba04439f6a7d61ffdf9b7abbd96a00908fb2.jpg"]
Image sharpness on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S was the single largest pain point raised in our post-launch debrief, accounting for the biggest part of your written feedback.

notes.title: Here is what we have worked on for this update

items.text: Visual Clarity & Anti-Aliasing: To reduce shimmering on fences and grass, we have implemented a dissolve effect and disabled an experimental anti-aliasing feature while continuing work on edge stability and texture passes.
Lighting Tweaks: We updated the general lighting by tweaking the night sky to improve overall balance and track visibility during night driving.

Headlight Throw: While headlight enhancements were initially targeted for this release, we are reallocating focus to ensure core lighting balance and shadow stability are rock-solid first; further headlight work remains in active development.
In our second debrief, we held a cautious line on multiplayer limits. Our instinct was to protect server tick rates by restricting private lobbies to 12 cars and 30-minute races.
Thanks to your clear feedback regarding league racing requirements, we re-evaluated our server limits and expanded our netcode infrastructure to support full 24-driver grids.
Grid Capacity: Custom Contests now support full 24-driver grids across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.
Session Durations: Race lengths can now be set up to 60 minutes, opening the door for genuine endurance stints and strategic pit windows.
Cross-platform server synchronisation and tick rates have been hardened to ensure pack racing remains clean from the green flag to the chequered flag.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/abbd6d2e93231d9a333ab54b748362161c5699ec.jpg"]
In this update, we addressed multiple issues where Quick Setup was not working properly for several wheel models on console platforms.
We will continue working on further improvements to wheel support and overall Force Feedback refinement in upcoming patches.

The in-session leaderboard has been updated to display more relevant real-time data while driving. Drivers can now toggle the display to view sector times, best lap times, and ideal laptimes, as well as monitor current tyre compound choices across the field.
We continue to iterate on AI racecraft, positioning logic, and predictability, using ongoing telemetry and community reports to drive continuous improvements.

Serious sim racing happens beyond the primary monitor. Whether it is external dashboard displays, wind simulators, tactile bass shakers, or button boxes, external hardware provides the physical feedback that connects you to the chassis.

We worked directly with the team at SimHub to build official, native telemetry output into the PC build. RENNSPORT now feeds high-frequency vehicle telemetry directly to SimHub without third-party workarounds or custom configuration scripts. Wire up your rigs, fire up your displays, and run your external hardware with complete confidence.
(Note: Requires the latest version of SimHub to function properly, please also note that this might not be available until Friday.)

releases.displayName: Patch Notes: Kings of the Ring DLC

items.text: Game Version: 1.2.15
Hello Racers,
This update focuses on strengthening the core foundation of RENNSPORT, shaped directly by the priorities you shared with us earlier this summer.
Alongside new content, this patch introduces initial refinements to Force Feedback, broader wheel hardware support, adjustments to the cockpit experience, and a wide array of stability fixes.

A significant portion of our work has centred on AI behaviour. Rather than promising perfection, our focus for this release is establishing a more reliable baseline. We have worked to eliminate erratic line changes, sudden braking on straights, and unprovoked contact. AI development remains an ongoing, iterative process that will continue well beyond this milestone, but this update represents a practical step towards our design target of smart racing and zero stupidity. We look forward to your grounded feedback once you have put laps in against the updated grid.
The Kings of the Ring DLC officially deploys tomorrow, 24th September. As previously confirmed, this expansion is included completely free for all owners of the Deluxe Edition.
To deploy the update, our servers will go offline tomorrow morning at 10:00 CEST for approximately three hours of scheduled maintenance.

notes.title: The Paid Content: a Homage to the Racing Community

items.text: Motorsport has never been polite. It is noisy, violent, and utterly indifferent to human hesitation. When you sit in the cockpit of a machine engineered to test physical limits, you either meet it with complete focus or it dismantles your confidence in the first corner.
With Kings of the Ring we’ve added three new machines that stake their claim on the asphalt, each with a legacy lovers of racing will appreciate.
Starting with a new King of the road.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/362147fe6ad3612ebb5c5daaa9ac1f2663e5fa97.jpg"]

Some machines follow sporting regulations; others exist solely to demonstrate what happens when engineers throw the rulebook into an incinerator. The 919 Evo is motorsport's apex predator, an unrestricted hybrid missile that reshaped our understanding of lap times at Spa and the Nordschleife. It is not merely fast. It operates in a regime of downforce and acceleration so violent that human reflexes struggle to keep pace.

Drivers who have strapped into the 919 Evo in our test builds all come back with the same wide-eyed look. The car does not float or slide. Ground effect and active aero clamp the carbon floor to the tarmac with tyrannical force. You brake at markers that your instincts swear will kill you, and you could swear that you felt the smell of burnt rubber, yet the hybrid powertrain and four-wheel drive haul the car through the apex before your brain has finished processing corner entry.

The 919 Evo demands absolute commitment. If you lift out of fear, you bleed downforce; if you stay flat, physics somehow bends to your will. It is an electrifying, breathless masterclass in modern engineering supremacy.

The Porsche 919 Hybrid Evo introduces an active Drag Reduction System (DRS). Engaging DRS trims the car's aerodynamic surfaces, dumping downforce and shedding drag to unlock a substantial increase in straight-line top speed down long straights like the Döttinger Höhe. Because trimming that downforce significantly reduces high-speed braking stability and grip, you will need to time your deployment carefully. Note that DRS is not automatic; you will need to bind the DRS action to a button on your wheel or controller in the settings menu before taking to the track.
We’re so convinced that once you’ve experienced driving it on the Nordschleife in RENNSPORT, it will put a smile on your face.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/faf1e25981276d933f0f8cfe1fcf1a3c0f403789.jpg"]

Developed for the iconic one-make championship supporting European Formula 1 rounds in 1979 and 1980, the BMW M1 Procar reflects a distinct era of analogue circuit racing. Powered by Paul Rosche’s naturally aspirated 3.5-litre M88/1 inline-six, the car delivers its power linearly and comes without modern driver aids, traction control, or ABS.

The mid-engine layout demands respect for basic chassis dynamics. Lap time comes from disciplined weight transfer on corner entry, measured downshifts to avoid locking the rear axle and smooth throttle modulation on exit. It is an honest, mechanical handling model that rewards clean inputs and precision over aggressive overdriving.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/dbb2ba9b23c41cd87f983d9fbfa850aafb746d99.jpg"]

Built around a carbon-fibre monocoque and powered by Audi’s 2.5-litre turbocharged five-cylinder engine, the KTM X-BOW GT2 represents a distinct design philosophy within the GT2 class. With a lower overall kerb weight than typical GT3 machinery, it relies on aerodynamic efficiency and power-to-weight performance rather than high downforce or large displacement.

On the circuit, the reduced mass translates to agile direction changes and direct feedback through the front axle. Finding consistent pace requires smooth steering inputs and disciplined throttle application to manage turbo boost on corner exit. It is a platform that rewards clean positioning, tidy lines, and carrying minimum corner speed rather than aggressive overdriving.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/f01532d3ec8e635e9764aab0835529fc946da5b6.jpg"]

There are racetracks, and then there is the Eifel forest. Sir Jackie Stewart did not coin the term "Green Hell" as a romantic experience; he said it because after winning the treacherous, fog- and rain-soaked 1968 German Grand Prix, he came up with the name because this place will bite your head off the moment your focus slips.

Over twenty kilometres of broken tarmac, blind crests, deceptive cambers, and zero run-off. It is the ultimate proving ground, an asphalt gauntlet where mechanical balance and driver grit are tested to destruction.

We already brought you the modern version of the Grand Prix circuit before, the Deluxe Edition drivers have battled day and night on the combined 24-Hour endurance layout. Now, we are serving up the beast in its purest, rawest form: the standalone Nordschleife, stripped clean of the Grand Prix loop. Just your machine, the curbs, and an unrelenting ribbon of tarmac daring you to keep your foot planted through Flugplatz and down the Döttinger Höhe (that's Döttinger Heights for us non-german-speaking folks).

notes.title: A quick word on how you get the keys

items.text: Deluxe Edition Owners get this standalone Nordschleife experience at zero extra cost. Consider it our salute to your early commitment; it drops straight into your garage as part of this pack (alongside the aforementioned cars, of course).
Standalone DLC Purchasers get the full pack, including this pure Nordschleife alongside full access to all pre-existing Nürburgring layouts, including the 24-Hour endurance configuration.
No half-measures. Strap in tight, trust your rear axle, and respect the forest.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/0c4d6e8b73de3d61e489b7f72793b6c0d8168c53.jpg"]

notes.title: The Free Content: a More Stable Baseline

items.text: Our mission has shifted slightly since the first half of this year. With our players’ feedback in the recent survey it was clear that we needed to address RENNSPORT’s fundamentals.
We agree that it’s not enough to keep adding new features and content on top of shaky grounds, so besides the content we are also addressing several of our community's requested topics.
Let’s talk about them!

notes.title: A New Baseline for Artificial Intelligence

items.text: Our design target for single-player racing remains focused on smart racing and zero stupidity. That means steadily eliminating erratic behaviour such as random braking on straights, sudden stops, and unprovoked collisions. For the Kings of the Ring update, the AI engineering team focused on establishing a solid baseline rather than declaring a finished product. Teaching computer-controlled cars to race convincingly takes steady iteration, and this release represents a practical step forward.

Competitors now show greater mutual respect for one another and for the player. The field exercises better spatial awareness when running in packs, giving more room during close-quarters racing and reducing unnecessary contact.

The AI adheres more consistently to optimal drivelines. Drivers now commit to full throttle when the track ahead is clear, which translates to cleaner launches off the grid and stronger straight-line pace, while remaining more measured and cautious as they navigate corners.

The team spent dedicated development time tuning behaviour across the difficulty settings, smoothing out the curve to provide a more consistent challenge. In addition, work went into refining how the AI behaves across our different car classes to ensure the competition feels appropriate to the vehicle you are driving.

Work on artificial intelligence remains an ongoing process that will continue well beyond this release. The team looks forward to your grounded feedback once you have put laps in against the updated field.

notes.title: Wheel base and Force Feedback Improvements

items.text: Following the feedback from Community Debrief #2, our hardware focus for this patch was on delivering more granular detail and removing artificial friction between your inputs and the car.

We recalibrated the baseline torque output curves for wheelbases on console platforms, with targeted tuning for PlayStation 5. This adjustment provides a broader dynamic range, allowing subtle front-tyre slip angles and kerb strikes to come through with greater clarity rather than clipping or feeling muffled.
We’ve also resolved an issue where certain third-party wheelbases and pedals were not recognised upon initial connection, ensuring your hardware is detected reliably on boot.

Additionally, we eliminated an artificial software delay previously present when rowing through gears on an external manual H-pattern shifter. Downshifts and upshifts now register the moment the physical gate is engaged.

In our recent debrief, drivers pointed out that cockpit visibility during dusk, dawn, and night sessions felt restrictive due to poor beam throw and hard shadow transitions. This patch introduces our first round of visual adjustments focused directly on track awareness from behind the wheel.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/a3babb1aed96a865800ad2ff1a3af369a9b539e8.jpg"]

We also have made an adjustment pass on ambient lighting and skybox values across daytime and nighttime conditions, tuning colour, saturation, and overall brightness. Shadow contrast was lifted slightly to recover detail in dark corners and cockpit interiors that previously felt crushed.

For night sessions, we reduced the intense headlight glare caused by cars behind you. Dashboards, and digital displays have been improved , though reflections on the windscreen and external side mirrors still require work in upcoming passes.

In addition, incorrect lighting modes across classic machinery (including the BMW M3 E30, Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 EVO II, Alfa Romeo 155 V6 TI, and HWA EVO.R) have been corrected for night competition.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/d7c061f474bcf3039e652706b63d199574d874ee.jpg"]

PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S can now toggle motion blur off in the graphics settings. Disabling this provides a crisper cockpit view, clearer mirror visibility, and cleaner edge definition through rapid direction changes.

Fair, dependable competition requires rules that enforce racecraft consistently across every split. We addressed several competitive loopholes and restrictions highlighted by our league hosts and daily racers.

The penalty logic for gaining an advantage off-track has been overhauled. Previously, the system only penalised a single position gained when cutting the circuit. The system now tracks and penalises every position gained while off the racing surface. Furthermore, off-track slowdown penalties in qualifying sessions are now served immediately rather than banking until the chequered flag.
High-ranked drivers with safety and skill ratings above 5000 are no longer inadvertently locked out of joining player-hosted Custom Contests.
Closed an exploit in competitive multiplayer sessions where players were able to switch to an exterior camera angle when the server host strictly mandated cockpit view.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/c2a53bcfec3a5826e59251dc89a0d2ba562c6c4f.jpg"]

releases.displayName: Patch Notes - Touring Classics Part 1 DLC

items.text: Hello racers!
We are excited to be back with a new expansion of RENNSPORT, featuring more content, bugfixes, and more!
The deployment of the Touring Classics Part 1 DLC will occur tomorrow morning at 09:00 CEST, servers are expected to be unavailable for approximately 3 hours.
We also have the 50 percent price cut coming out tomorrow, alongside the update.
We are happy to deliver on what our community wanted the most: content. There’s a lot to unpack. So let’s dig into what this expansion holds!

There is a specific kind of violence inherent in 90s touring cars. These were not software-assisted commutes; they were raw, mechanical, and uncompromising machines that demanded everything from the driver.

Tomorrow, that intensity comes to RENNSPORT with the Touring Classics Part 1 expansion. The servers will become unavailable at 09:00 CEST tomorrow morning, and we expect the deployment to take approximately 3 hours time.
Before we talk about steel, let’s talk about the barrier to entry.
We are cutting the price of the RENNSPORT Standard Edition by 50 percent, effective tomorrow.
The grid needs more cars, and the racing is better when the field is deep. Look for similar adjustments to the Deluxe Edition during the summer sale at the end of July.
Expanding the roster and widening the gate is important to us, because it is important for our RENNSPORT community. Let’s talk about the details!
The centerpiece of this update is a digital reconstruction of the legendary Hockenheimring forest layout—the circuit purged by FIA safety mandates in 2002.

Imagine the re-opening of this infamous sector was greenlit today, allowing the modern GP course to once again bleed into those terrifying, ultra-high-speed forest straights that defined decades of Touring Classics and Formula 1 history.
We have effectively done just that. Here, no regulations or safety concerns hold back the intensity.

We have meticulously blended the historic layout with our modern infrastructure; while it should be stated that this isn’t an exact replica of the original, the soul of the circuit remains untouched. It is long, lethal, and blind. You are essentially stepping into a time machine that ignores the compromises of the present. Treat the forest with respect, or it will claim you.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/c1c6e499e6aca4395a54224d17de3c9af885f885.jpg"]
These machines represent the peak of the Touring Classics engineering arms race. No assists, no fluff—just metal and intent.
Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evo II: The "Cosworth." It’s an exercise in flared aggression and mechanical feedback. If you can’t feel the grip through the wheel, you aren't pushing hard enough.
BMW E30 M3: The icon. The S14 engine is a scalpel, and the chassis balance is the industry gold standard. It is nimble, communicative, and will punish you if you get greedy.

Alfa Romeo 155 V6 TI: An Italian anomaly. With an advanced all-wheel-drive system and a ferocious V6, this car doesn't turn—it claws. You have to commit early and let the mechanical grip pull you through the chaos.
Mercedes-Benz C-Class V6 DTM: A technological brute. With a high-revving V6 and aero that sticks the car to the asphalt, this was the pinnacle of mid-90s excess.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/1da7ec1c0e0edd7c35ace78bcd2cc2d9bc67ed5b.jpg"]

notes.title: A Canvas for Competition: The Livery Expansion

items.text: We heard you loud and clear: you want the ability to express your identity on track. Lino has been working around the clock to deliver a massive visual overhaul to our vehicle roster. This update brings a staggering volume of new liveries to the platform:
Touring Classics Heritage: We are including 20 bespoke Touring Classics-inspired liveries across our four new touring cars, completely free for all owners of this DLC.
RENNSPORT Cup Collection: We are adding 348 unique RENNSPORT Cup liveries across 29 different vehicles, available for 50 RENN$ each.
Hall of Fame: We are also introducing 8 exclusive Hall of Fame liveries for our GT3 fleet, reserved for the elite few who prove their mettle by winning our official RENNSPORT leagues and events.
But that’s not all, we have more stuff coming in this expansion, let’s move on to the free stuff that we’ve added to The Touring Classics Part 1!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/217a908972f43bf89f33303a93ac7c66e0e71919.jpg"]

notes.title: The Free Expansion: Thermalito & New Iron

items.text: We are also opening the doors to Thermalito. Originally a community mod by DDF Racer, we have partnered with Nukedrop to polish this circuit into the official RENNSPORT fold. It lacks the laser-scanned clinical perfection of our main tracks, but it compensates with pure, technical flow. It’s a scrappy, honest playground that demands precision over horsepower.
HWA EVO.R: A modern nod to the Touring Classics spirit, born to conquer the Green Hell. A modern interpretation of the 190E.
Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Clubsport: A mid-engine lesson in balance. It provides a modern, high-downforce contrast to the twitchy legends of the 90s.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/084a2d20c6fc426109304db3a0132f566d29e5c1.jpg"]
While we continue to work on the AI, Rikard, Daniel, and the engineering team have made adjustments to the AI in the latest build.

We aren't calling this a "new iteration" yet, but the difference on track is noticeable. Our focus has been on refinement, and making the AI drivers feel like a coherent part of the race, continuing our improvements to the single player experience.
The AI driving logic has been tweaked across these categories:
Collision Awareness: The AI now takes greater consideration to avoid contact with both human drivers and their fellow AI competitors.
Cornering Logic: They are better at calculating braking zones and trajectory through curves, resulting in a cleaner, more fluid line and fewer unnecessary spin-outs.

Pit Lane Professionalism: The AI now navigates pit entry, exit, and lane speed limits with significantly improved behavior.

We chose this Touring Classics era because it was the last time the driver, not the software, dictated the outcome. These cars are loud, they are twitchy, and they are unforgiving. If you get greedy, the forest or the gravel will humble you.

We are adding content and expanding the technical playground. By cutting the entry price in half, we are opening the garage doors to a wider field of drivers. Whether you are hunting apexes at the Hockenheimring Classic Revival or finding your rhythm in the Cayman at Thermalito, this is a test of mechanical sympathy and raw commitment.
The machine park is growing, the pricing is more accessible, you have more options to visually customize your car, the single-player experience has improved, and the grid is waiting.
The only thing missing is you in the driver’s seat.

releases.displayName: Coming Tomorrow: The Free Coast to Coast Update

items.text: Hello Racers!

Our recent community survey received well over 400+ detailed responses. We are incredibly grateful for the feedback and the raw honesty you provided. Our first official Community Debrief is coming out this Friday for your reading.
In that brief, we will step directly under the spotlight to discuss exactly what you told us, how we are prioritizing your feedback, and the concrete actions we are taking to fix the foundation.

One narrative stood out above all others in the survey data. Our racing community wants more content to expand the competitive footprint of the sim, and you want solid improvements to the AI. We hear you, and we are reacting immediately.
Tomorrow at 09:00 CEST, we are deploying the free Coast to Coast Update.
This free update brings you AI-improvements, two new tracks (Laguna Seca, and Sebring), and additional bugfixes.

You will notice that the Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Clubsport is not included. We made a deliberate operational choice here. Following the technical bottlenecks that delayed our last major release, we refuse to hold back completed assets from our drivers, instead we are adding the second iteration of the AI (more info below).

To execute this deployment, the servers will temporarily go offline tomorrow, Thursday, June 11, at 09:00 CEST. The estimated downtime for maintenance and update propagation will be approximately 3 hours.

As we mentioned recently, our previous approach to discounts has been inconsistent. We have struggled to align dates across storefronts, and platform restrictions have prevented us from delivering the deals we intended.
Rather than fighting these constraints, we are changing the model.

Effective Friday, 19th June, the base price of the RENNSPORT Standard Edition will be permanently reduced by 50%. This bypasses the need for platform-specific discount slots and ensures that everyone, regardless of where they play, gets the same entry price immediately. We are delivering on the commitment we made at the Munich Summit: to offer double the content at half the price.
We will continue to manage discounts on other content as individual platform constraints allow, but the barrier to entry for the Standard Edition is now settled and predictable.
We are systematically stripping away the limitations of our legacy code. This update introduces a more capable field of opponents:

Performance Decoupling: We have done work to transition critical segments of our AI logic to be framerate-independent. This helps ensure that opponent behaviour remains more consistent regardless of your hardware performance or display settings.
Velocity and Aggression: You will notice a marked increase in overall AI pace. Opponents are now more confident at the limit and faster across the entire lap.
Track Discipline: We have refined the pathing logic to ensure AI drivers stay within the circuit boundaries, drastically reducing the frequency of erratic excursions into the grass.

Behavioral Stability: We have eliminated the "phantom braking" bug that caused AI cars to slam on the anchors without cause. While this was most visible on the Daytona Oval, this is a systemic fix that will improve race flow across all circuits.

Banking Awareness: We corrected the trajectory logic for banked circuits. Opponents on the Daytona Tri-Oval now maintain a safe, racing-appropriate line, eliminating the friction and wall-scraping that plagued the previous build.

Our focus on AI improvements stems directly from your survey feedback. We acknowledge ongoing issues with AI collisions, particularly on Sebring and Nordschleife, and have already begun work on the next iteration.

True simulation requires circuits that test the structural limits of a chassis and the psychological resolve of the driver. This update delivers two of the most uncompromising tracks in North America.

Nestled in Monterey, California, this circuit is defined by elevation change and high-risk braking zones. The focal point is the iconic Corkscrew. Dropping 18 metres in a blind, left-right alternation, it requires absolute precision on entry and a willingness to trust your sensory inputs over your vision. One mistake here completely invalidates your stint.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/af9cd627b88ec175a698b07757ae7b16ce271fa6.jpg"]

Built on the concrete slabs of a former military airfield, Sebring is an unyielding test of endurance engineering. The track surface transitions violently between modern asphalt and legacy concrete. Managing vehicle balance over the brutal bumps of Sunset Bend requires a highly progressive force feedback profile and respect for tire carcass deflection. It is a track that breaks fragile components.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45136077/b84a3526c86aa4c7fad19f209fcda130dd2ea05b.jpg"]

This update marks our second major architectural iteration on the AI systems. We are moving away from rigid, frame-dependent behaviours toward a more fluid, intelligent opponent model. This release is a direct result of the raw telemetry data and feedback we gathered during your races over the past weeks.

Hello Racers,
We’re excited to finally bring you the Endurance Classics 1!

This update represents a pivotal moment for RENNSPORT. We are delivering a massive expansion of content alongside foundational improvements to the racing experience. From the legendary Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans to the grit of the Kuala Lumpur Street Circuit, this update marks a major step toward our goal of doubling the amount of content available in RENNSPORT throughout 2026.
01 // The Core Focus: Multiplayer foundations and the single-player transition.
02 // A New AI Architecture: First iteration details and operational context.
03 // Championship Mode: Playlists, scoring overhauls, and leaderboards.
04 // Custom Contests: Community league tools and event customization.
05 // Competition Standards: Track limit refinements and physical shifting support.
06 // Visual Overhaul: Atmospheric lighting and environmental rendering updates.
07 // The Legend of Le Mans: Full breakdown of paid and free content.
08 // Technical Changelog: Comprehensive stability, physics, and hardware data.
This update brings a massive wave of improvements to RENNSPORT, focusing on a more immersive, fair, and thrilling racing experience for both single- and multiplayer.

RENNSPORT is, and will continue to be built on the foundation of competitive online multiplayer racing. We are handing the keys of the circuit to you with the introduction of Custom Contests. This feature allows community leaders and leagues to create their own online events with total control over their settings from car restrictions, to rating limits, and track selections.

This update also marks the beginning of our journey to provide an enhanced single-player experience with a massive overhaul of our AI, which is one among multiple improvements to the Championship Mode.
But wait, there’s more! We’re adding 5 new cars, more than 20 new free liveries, new track layouts, visual enhancements to the game, countless stability fixes, and more!

Whether you are a solo driver climbing the ranks or a community leader hosting events, there is something in this update for everyone. Let’s dig into the full content of this significant update, starting with our fresh first iteration of the new AI.

We have fundamentally re-engineered how you compete against the computer. The previous system fell short of our standards, so we chose to rebuild the logic from the ground up. This foundational release introduces opponents that understand space, aggression, and the physical consequences of a collision.

Rikard, our lead engineer on this system, was hesitant to release this logic until it reached his definition of absolute completion. However, we believe the most effective way to refine this intelligence is to get it onto the track and iterate based on your feedback.
This system is a "First Iteration." We are currently tracking several specific behaviours that will be addressed in upcoming patches:
Acceleration at the Start: The AI currently prioritises safety over raw aggression off the line. You may notice they do not accelerate with full force initially to ensure a clean start for the field.
Wobbling and Pathing: Under certain car and track combinations, opponents may display a "wobbling" effect as they calculate the optimal racing line.
Positional Braking: On high-speed sections like Eau Rouge at Spa or the high banks of Daytona, the AI may occasionally slow down or lift "unreasonably" as it works to avoid collisions.
Track Limit Excursions: There are instances where the AI may leave the track limits unexpectedly while defending or navigating heavy traffic.
The GT3 Standard: This system is primary-tested for GT3 machinery. Performance in other classes will vary as we continue to calibrate their unique physics.
Simulation Frequency: AI performance is tied to your framerate. For the most consistent intelligence, we recommend maintaining a stable 60+ FPS.
The Path Forward
This is a new baseline for our single-player experience. The previous code had reached the limit of its potential; by starting fresh, we have given ourselves a platform that can finally grow.
This new system is more flexible, allowing for more dynamic adjustments and rapid improvements based on your feedback.
Our single-player progression has been improved to give you a clearer sense of achievement. The updated Championship Mode has been improved over in the following ways:
Introducing Playlists: Instead of being locked into "Rookie" or "Pro" tiers, Championships are now grouped into Playlists, allowing you to dive into the content you love most.
Championship Score: We’ve traded Medals for a new Score system, giving you a more granular way to track your performance.
Global Leaderboards: See where you stand against the world’s best with newly added leaderboards for all Championships.

For our multiplayer fans, we are handing you the keys to the circuit. This has been a highly requested feature, and we’re adding it into this update. Custom Contests allow you to create your own online events with total control.
Total Customization: Set your own rating limits, car restrictions, track selections, and timelines.
Community Focused: Perfect for leagues or friends who want to race under specific conditions.
This gives you a solid system to set up your own multiplayer leagues, which automates a lot of the tasks for you.
We heard your feedback! Track limits across all circuits have been tuned to be more consistent.
Community-Driven: Adjustments were made based on where you felt the "line" should be.
Consistency is Key: You can now push the car to the limit with a clearer understanding of where the penalties begin.

For the purists who love the mechanical feel of a gear shift, this update is for you. We have officially added support for H-Pattern and Sequential hardware shifters. Whether you’re rowing through gears in a classic or clicking through a modern box, the car will now respond to your physical hardware.
The world of RENNSPORT has never looked better. We’ve tweaked our rendering to create a more cinematic and realistic atmosphere.
Stunning Skies: Experience more vibrant sunsets, improved cloud formations, and better lighting transitions.
Cinematic Polish: We’ve added lens flares and increased contrast for a "big-screen" feel.
Realistic Details: Grass and gravel now have more physically accurate colors, and we’ve boosted headlight strength to help you navigate those darker, high-contrast nights.

items.text: Endurance racing is the ultimate test of mechanical discipline and psychological focus. To honor that heritage, this update introduces a selection of machinery and circuits that have shaped the history of motorsport.

The inclusion of the Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans introduces a completely different type of challenge to the platform. This is not a circuit where you simply chase a single qualifying lap; it requires a deep understanding of slipstreaming, tire management, and maintaining focus through changing track conditions. Navigating the Mulsanne straight at night requires patience and absolute respect for the limits of your hardware.

To complement this environment, the vehicle roster spans multiple generations of high-performance engineering. The selection bridges the gap between the raw, ground-effect power of the Group C era, the high-downforce peak of late-90s GT1 machinery, and the sophisticated electronics of modern prototypes and GT3 fields. This diversity provides a stark contrast in weight distribution, power delivery, and aerodynamic behavior, giving purists a thorough test of driver skill.

Alongside our core endurance additions, we are expanding the foundational platform with a mix of street circuits, alternative layouts, and forward-looking concepts available to all drivers at no additional cost.

Thank you for the immediate feedback and issue reports following the launch of Endurance Classics Part 1. Your first-hand experience that you have shared with us in the survey and across our social media channels has allowed our engineering team to quickly isolate several friction points. Today we deployed version 1.2.5 to address some of the immediate issues.
The development team is already hard at work on an additional patch to tackle more of the issues that you have shared with us. That patch will deploy as soon as it is done.
Here are the full patch notes for our first hotfix for Endurance Classics Part 1:
Resolved a rare issue where AI cars could become invisible but still be involved in collisions, eliminating phantom obstacles on the track.
Stability Improvement: Addressed the excessively long loading times on the Nordschleife circuit that caused players to disconnect before entering the track.
Custom Contest Access: Elite drivers can now join custom contests: users with a Rennsport Rating over 5000 can now participate.
Crash Fix: Eliminated a crash that occasionally occurred while loading into a custom contest.
Auto-Skip: Races will now automatically be skipped if you receive a black flag in qualification for driving the wrong direction.
Simulation Fix: Ensured that skipping practice or qualifying properly calculates and simulates AI lap times.
The size of championship logos has been increased on the reward screen for improved visibility.
Corrected an issue where the rank progress bar displayed the wrong information for the next tier.
Resolved a problem where images for various championship playlists sometimes failed to load.
UI Cleanup: Fixed a duplicate entry of “Practice” appearing when editing session settings.
PS5 Controller Reliability: The PS5 gamepad is now correctly recognized after being disconnected and reconnected while the “Gamepad Disconnected” pop-up is shown.
Wheel Setup: Corrected an initial setup issue that resulted in inverted paddle shifter inputs.
Minimap Accuracy: The finish line position has been corrected on the minimaps for both Goodwood and Nürburgring GP.

Leaderboard Time Correction: Fixed the Total Time display on leaderboards. It now accurately reflects the time taken to finish the race, resolving a bug where winning players appeared slower than the AI.
Platform Polish: General spelling errors have been corrected on the PS5 platform.
Results Panel: Penalty numbers now correctly appear in the results panel after completing a race in Custom Contest or Championship modes.
Reminder Widget: Added a checkmark and bell icon to the reminder widget.
Fuel Alert Consistency: The Fuel alert widget now has the correct default placement, icon, and color.
Track Logo Scaling: Corrected the size of the Kuala Lumpur track logo, which was previously too large.
Visual Update: The design of the pitbox info widget has been updated.
Menu Visibility: Resolved an issue where the XP gained (level up) UI would overlap with the background main menu when returning from Time Trial.
Quick Play Status: The “Searching for Drivers” text no longer persists on the player list after a player cancels a Find a Race search in Quick Play mode.
Hockenheimring GP: Missing white lines have been added at Turn 2 and the hairpin.
Le Mans: Fixed an issue where the wrong background image was being used for the track.
Car Performance: Resolved a bug where the Peugeot 9X8's battery drained too quickly.
Vehicle Physics: Updated the baseline setups and performed a physics pass for all LMDh cars.

A new League Points System has been implemented.
Results from all splits are now merged into a single ranking, and points are awarded based on each driver’s position in this combined list.
The points for the first (winner of the highest split) and last (last placed player in the lowest split) drivers are determined by the total number of registrations.
3 or fewer registrations: no points are awarded.
4 or more registrations: the winner’s points gradually increase up to a maximum of 200 points, which is reached when there are 18 or more registrations.
The last-placed driver always receives 1 point, as long as there are at least 4 entries.
Points for every other position are then interpolated between the winner’s and last driver’s points using predefined relative distances, which determine the gaps between positions.
Drivers who do not finish the race or get disqualified are ineligible for points.

This system is a "First Iteration." We are currently tracking several specific behaviours that will be addressed in upcoming patches:
Acceleration at the Start: The AI currently prioritises safety over raw aggression off the line. You may notice they do not accelerate with full force initially to ensure a clean start for the field.
Wobbling and Pathing: Under certain car and track combinations, opponents may display a "wobbling" effect as they calculate the optimal racing line.
Positional Braking: On high-speed sections like Eau Rouge at Spa or the high banks of Daytona, the AI may occasionally slow down or lift "unreasonably" as it works to avoid collisions.
Track Limit Excursions: There are instances where the AI may leave the track limits unexpectedly while defending or navigating heavy traffic.
The GT3 Standard: This system is primary-tested for GT3 machinery. Performance in other classes will vary as we continue to calibrate their unique physics.
Simulation Frequency: AI performance is tied to your framerate. For the most consistent intelligence, we recommend maintaining a stable 60+ FPS.
The Path Forward
This is a new baseline for our single-player experience. The previous code had reached the limit of its potential; by starting fresh, we have given ourselves a platform that can finally grow.
This new system is more flexible, allowing for more dynamic adjustments and rapid improvements based on your feedback.
